title: You wake up somewhere. You have 60 seconds to figure out where.
sources: NASA Mars facts: gravity ~38% of Earth's, average temperature about -60 C (-80 F), atmosphere under 1% of Earth's pressure, mostly CO2: https://science.nasa.gov/mars/facts/
Mars is ~1.52 AU from the Sun, so the Sun looks about two-thirds as wide as from Earth.
NASA, vacuum exposure: don't hold your breath (lung damage); ~10-15 s of useful consciousness. Jim LeBlanc's 1966 vacuum chamber accident: he felt saliva bubbling on his tongue.
At Mars surface pressure (~0.6 kPa), water boils near 0 C.

shots.text: You wake up. You have no idea where you are.
And you've got about one minute of air in your lungs.
Clue one. The sky is orange. Like old butterscotch.
Clue two. You jump, and you go almost three times higher than normal.
Clue three. It's minus sixty degrees.
shots.say: Clue three. It's minus sixty degrees.

shots.text: But your water bottle is boiling.
Clue four. The spit on your tongue starts to fizz.
Comment your guess. Right now. Before the last clue.
Last clue. The Sun is smaller than it should be. And it's setting.
And you're doing the one thing that'll kill you fastest. Holding your breath.
Out here, held air tears your lungs. Breathe out. Now.
That buys you about fifteen seconds. Then you see it. A door. Forty metres away.
Would you make it? Send this to the friend who wouldn't.

label.text: SEND TO THE FRIEND WHO WOULDN'T
